_note: HAND-BUILT SAMPLE, schema-accurate but not generated by a live request: FastAPI has never been installable in this build sandbox (see docs/api_surveillance.md), so no HTTP server has run here. Every field name and type below is copied verbatim from app/api/v1/ai.py's AskResponse/CitationOut Pydantic models. The citation structure, the [T#]/[D#] marker scheme, and the re-scoping-to-the-flagged-disease behavior are real and covered by tests/ai/test_workflow.py, tests/ai/test_citation.py and tests/ai/test_prompts.py against fakes; the exact wording of `answer` here is illustrative, since it depends on a live Gemini call this sandbox cannot make.

body.question: What's going around right now, and how do I protect myself?

request_example.note: disease is left null on purpose here: naming a disease explicitly would skip the automatic currently-flagged-signal lookup and the question would be answered about only that disease.

response_example.answer: Dengue is currently flagged as elevated in Sindh, Pakistan [T1]. To protect yourself: eliminate standing water around your home where mosquitoes breed, use an EPA/locally-approved insect repellent, wear long sleeves and trousers, and use window and door screens or bed nets, since dengue spreads through daytime-biting Aedes mosquitoes [D2]. Seek medical care promptly for high fever, severe headache, or bleeding, and avoid aspirin or other NSAIDs for a fever that could be dengue, since they can worsen bleeding risk; use paracetamol/acetaminophen instead unless a clinician advises otherwise [D2].

citations.label: Dengue (WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean) (World Health Organization)

limitations: The disease discussed was selected automatically from currently flagged surveillance signals [T#], not named by the question; ask about a specific disease for a more targeted answer.

insufficient_evidence_example.answer: I don't have enough retrieved evidence to answer this reliably. Please check the surveillance dashboard directly, or ask a more specific question (disease, country, time period) so I can look for matching observations and documents.
limitations: No evidence was available for this question.
